title: Istanbul to Edirne by Train: How the Çerkezköy Transfer Works
excerpt: The new Çerkezköy–Kapıkule high-speed line makes a rail day trip to Edirne realistic, but it starts with a transfer outside Istanbul. Here is how to plan it.

body.text: Edirne, with its Ottoman mosques and covered bazaars, has long been a classic side trip from Istanbul. Since October 2026 there is a new way to get there: the Çerkezköy–Kapıkule section of the Halkalı–Kapıkule high-speed railway has opened to passengers. The headline is attractive, but the practical detail matters more for a visitor. The new high-speed trains do not yet start in Istanbul. For now, a rail trip to Edirne is a two-part journey with a planned connection at Çerkezköy. This guide explains what has opened, what has not, and how to decide whether the train suits your day.

According to the [Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure](https://www.uab.gov.tr/haberler/halkali-kapikule-arasi-hizli-trenle-1-5-saate-duesecek/), the full Halkalı–Kapıkule project is about 229 km long. The 153 km Çerkezköy–Kapıkule section is the first and longest stage, built as a double-track electrified line designed for 200 km/h. The Istanbul end of the corridor, between Ispartakule and Çerkezköy, was still under construction when the ministry reported on the project in June 2026. Its long-term projection is a Halkalı–Kapıkule passenger journey of about 1.5 hours, compared with roughly four hours before the project.

Launch reporting on 10 October 2026 described high-speed trains running between Çerkezköy and Edirne, stopping at Büyükkarıştıran, Lüleburgaz and Babaeski, with the minister citing a Çerkezköy–Edirne time of 54 minutes. Passengers from Halkalı were described as taking a regional train to Çerkezköy and changing there. Treat these as launch details, not a timetable: the departure list for your date is the only reliable plan.

items: Leg 1 — your hotel to Halkalı. Halkalı is on Istanbul’s European side, far west of the historic centre. Allow generous time, particularly from the Asian side.
Leg 2 — the regional train from Halkalı to Çerkezköy. This is the existing conventional line, so it is slower than the new section.
Leg 3 — the high-speed train from Çerkezköy to Edirne, followed by the local journey from Edirne’s station to the places you want to see.

body.text: Build the day backwards from the return. Find the last sensible high-speed departure from Edirne that connects with a regional train back to Halkalı, then decide how much of Edirne you can realistically see before it. A connection that looks comfortable on paper can feel tight with a group, luggage or an unfamiliar station.

items: Confirm on the operator’s channels, starting at [TCDD Taşımacılık](https://www.tcddtasimacilik.gov.tr/), that both legs run on your date and in both directions.
Check whether the two legs are sold as one journey or as separate tickets, and what happens to the second leg if the first runs late.
Note the full station names. Edirne’s new high-speed station may not be next to the sights you plan to visit, so map the last kilometres before you go.
Compare the complete hotel-to-Edirne time with the familiar alternatives, such as an intercity coach or a private driver.
Keep a fallback for the evening return so a missed connection does not leave you improvising late at night.

body.text: Who the train suits — and who should wait

The rail option suits travellers who enjoy the journey itself, are staying on the European side near the western rail corridor, or want to see Lüleburgaz or Babaeski along the way. It is less attractive for a first visit with only one free day, or for anyone staying in Sultanahmet or Kadıköy, where the trip to Halkalı adds a substantial first leg. In those cases a direct road transfer may still give you more hours in Edirne. When the Istanbul section opens, the calculation will change, and a one-seat rail ride will be far easier to recommend.

If you are new to the city’s network, our [Istanbul public transport guide](/blog/istanbul-public-transport-tourist-guide) explains how to reach the main rail hubs. For a comparable intercity rail decision in the opposite direction, see our [Istanbul–Ankara high-speed train checklist](/blog/istanbul-ankara-yht-booking-checklist). And if Edirne is competing with other day trips, our [three-, five- and seven-day Istanbul itinerary](/blog/istanbul-itinerary-3-5-7-days) helps you weigh what to give up.

Kapıkule sits at Türkiye’s border with Bulgaria, and the project is part of a wider European rail corridor. The opening of this section is not the same as a new international passenger service. If you are thinking of continuing into Bulgaria by rail, confirm with the operators what is actually bookable for your date rather than relying on the name of the line.

seo.intent: Decide whether to reach Edirne from Istanbul by the new high-speed rail section and how to plan the Halkalı–Çerkezköy connection.
seo.uniqueValue: A three-leg planning method and five pre-booking checks for the new Çerkezköy–Kapıkule section; separates what opened in October 2026 from the unfinished Istanbul section and from international services.

quality.reviewNotes: Prepared 2026-10-24. Facts checked against the Transport Ministry project page (229 km, 153 km first stage, Ispartakule–Çerkezköy under construction in June 2026, 1.5 h projection) and CNBC-e launch report of 10 Oct 2026 (stations, 54 min, Halkalı transfer). Exact departure times and fares deliberately omitted; operator homepage linked for checking, not cited as evidence. No border-entry guidance given. Independent review recorded in the daily ledger.
